office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 45th District (Kirkland, Redmond, Woodinville, Sammamish, Duvall), serving two-year terms writing state law and budgets.
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Roger Goodman, in the House since 2007 and chair of the Community Safety Committee, faces Republican JoAnn Tolentino, a retired music teacher and compliance professional making her first legislative run. Goodman took 72.87% in the August primary.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2007 and chair of the House Community Safety Committee; attorney and former director of the state Sentencing Guidelines Commission.
highlights: Cites laws on crime survivors, drug and mental health services, and police accountability and training [S1]
Voted yes on ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal [S6]
Voted yes on ESHB 1296, the 2025 parental-rights amendments that I-1 would undo [S5]
Pledges to champion K-12 funding, affordable housing investments, climate action and reproductive rights [S1]

experience.basis: House member since 2007 and chair of the Community Safety Committee, citing an enacted record.

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 millionaires' tax; his statement stresses tax relief for working people and small businesses rather than new revenue.

spending.basis: Cites free school meals and childcare funding and pledges K-12 and affordable-housing investment.

safety.basis: Record and platform center on police accountability reform and expanded drug and mental health services, alongside crime-survivor protections.

climate.basis: Pledges to champion climate action; primary-era campaign material cited carbon-cap legislation.

housing.basis: Pledges continued affordable-housing investments; no deregulation or rent-policy statement.

social.basis: Single explicit pledge to champion reproductive rights.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yes on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Republican challenger from Woodinville, a retired music teacher and compliance-software professional and five-year precinct committee officer, running as "not a politician."
highlights: Says "parents, not politicians, should guide their children's education and healthcare" [S3]
Supports voter ID, paper ballots and bipartisan election oversight [S1][S3]
Would fight regulations driving up housing costs and streamline permitting and zoning [S1][S3]
Backs fossil fuels, nuclear and hydro to keep energy bills low [S3]

experience.basis: No public office beyond precinct committee officer; presents herself as "not a politician."

parental-rights.basis: Repeated statements: "empower parents"; parents "should guide their children's education and healthcare"; involve parents and reject CRT and gender-ideology content in classrooms.

local-control.basis: Calls to "restore local control" in schools, a single statement.

housing.basis: Would fight regulations driving up housing costs and streamline permitting and zoning to build more homes.

climate.basis: Champions affordable energy and supports fossil fuels, nuclear and hydro "to keep bills low."

safety.basis: "Full support for our law enforcement" paired with "treatment, not just punishment" and recovery programs.

spending.basis: "Audit every dollar and pass balanced budgets"; waste and fraud and fiscal accountability are recurring themes.

immigration.basis: Supports legal immigration, the rule of law and border security, with "humane processing."
